used Jev to classify 1,018 AI research papers.

The result: $0.08 total cost and 256ms median end-to-end latency per paper.

The pipeline was:

1. Summarize each paper with DeepSeek V4 Flash
2. Send the title + summary + 24 possible topics to Jev
3. Use Jev to classify each paper
4. Visualize everything on https://t.co/hs63SlHxjw

The summaries cost $3.99 on @togethercompute. The classifications cost $0.08 on @typesafeai.

So for just over $4 of inference, I ended up with a pretty useful way to explore the top AI research papers from the past year.

I think this is where things are heading: different models for different parts of the workflow, instead of using one model for everything.

I’m running evals on the Jev classifications before replacing the current ones, but the site is already live: https://t.co/hs63SlHxjw&quot;</h1><!--$?--><template id="B:0"></template><!--$--><div whitespace-pre-wrap break-words text-text text-body font-normal"><span class="font-chirp max-w-full whitespace-pre-wrap break-words text-inherit text-[length:inherit] font-inherit">I used Jev to classify 1,018 AI research papers.

The result: $0.08 total cost and 256ms median end-to-end latency per paper.

The pipeline was:

1. Summarize each paper with DeepSeek V4 Flash
2. Send the title + summary + 24 possible topics to Jev
3. Use Jev to classify each paper
4. Visualize everything on </span><a class="font-chirp max-w-full whitespace-pre-wrap break-words text-brand text-[length:inherit] font-inherit hover:underline" href="http://1kpapers.com" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">1kpapers.com</a><span class="font-chirp max-w-full whitespace-pre-wrap break-words text-inherit text-[length:inherit] font-inherit">

The summaries cost $3.99 on </span><a class="rounded-xs focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-ring hover:underline max-w-full text-[length:inherit] font-[inherit] text-brand" href="/togethercompute">@<!-- -->togethercompute</a><span class="font-chirp max-w-full whitespace-pre-wrap break-words text-inherit text-[length:inherit] font-inherit">. The classifications cost $0.08 on </span><a class="rounded-xs focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-ring hover:underline max-w-full text-[length:inherit] font-[inherit] text-brand" href="/typesafeai">@<!-- -->typesafeai</a><span class="font-chirp max-w-full whitespace-pre-wrap break-words text-inherit text-[length:inherit] font-inherit">.

So for just over $4 of inference, I ended up with a pretty useful way to explore the top AI research papers from the past year.

I think this is where things are heading: different models for different parts of the workflow, instead of using one model for everything.

I’m running evals on the Jev classifications before replacing the current ones, but the site is already live: </span><a class="font-chirp max-w-full whitespace-pre-wrap break-words text-brand text-[length:inherit] font-inherit hover:underline" href="http://1kpapers.com" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">1kpapers.com</a></div><div class="flex flex-col gap-1 empty:hidden"><div classify 1,018 AI research papers.

The result: $0.08 total cost and 256ms median end-to-end latency per paper.

The pipeline was:

1. Summarize each paper with DeepSeek V4 Flash
2. Send the title + summary + 24 possible topics to Jev
3. Use Jev to classify each paper
4. Visualize everything on </span><a class="font-chirp max-w-full whitespace-pre-wrap break-words text-brand text-[length:inherit] font-inherit hover:underline" href="http://1kpapers.com" rel="noopener noreferrer" target="_blank">1kpapers.com</a><span class="font-chirp max-w-full whitespace-pre-wrap break-words text-inherit text-[length:inherit] font-inherit">

The summaries cost $3.99 on </span><a class="rounded-xs focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-ring hover:underline max-w-full text-[length:inherit] font-[inherit] text-brand" href="/togethercompute">@<!-- -->togethercompute</a><span class="font-chirp max-w-full whitespace-pre-wrap break-words text-inherit text-[length:inherit] font-inherit">. The classifications cost $0.08 on </span><a class="rounded-xs focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-ring hover:underline max-w-full text-[length:inherit] font-[inherit] text-brand" href="/typesafeai">@<!-- -->typesafeai</a><span class="font-chirp max-w-full whitespace-pre-wrap break-words text-inherit text-[length:inherit] font-inherit">.

So for just over $4 of inference, I ended up with a pretty useful way to explore the top AI research papers from the past year.

I think this is where things are heading: different models for different parts of the workflow, instead of using one model for everything.

I’m running evals on the Jev classifications before replacing the current ones, but the site is already live: </span><a class="font-chirp max-w-full whitespace-pre-wrap break-words text-brand
